claims.claim: The 1992 RSVP experiment observed degraded second-probe detection during a 270ms window starting about 180ms after T1.
claims.limitation: Cannot generalize timing as brain shutdown.

claims.claim: Identification of T1, task instructions and blank interval affect second probe performance.
claims.limitation: Experimental paradigm.

claims.claim: Lag-1 sparing occurs in some sequences and can coexist with temporal-order errors.
claims.limitation: Stimulus and outcome dependence.

claims.claim: Working-memory vs attentional-selection explanation remains debated.
claims.limitation: Do not assert a settled single mechanism.

claims.claim: T1-difficulty magnifies the blink in all paradigms.
claims.limitation: 2021 study challenges broad generalization.

claims.claim: The 2007 meditation study involved 17 practitioners, 23 novices and intensive 3-month retreat.
claims.limitation: Not randomized audio-product trial.

claims.claim: Intensive retreat group showed smaller attentional blink and reduced P3b to T1.
claims.limitation: Not proof of everyday productivity or Zen12.

claims.claim: EEG theta activity can inform mechanisms of second-target detection after training.
claims.limitation: Do not infer proprietary binaural effect.

claims.claim: RSVP attention engagement in 2023 experiments showed tens-of-ms timing costs.
claims.limitation: Not applicable to unmeasured everyday activities.

claims.claim: The attentional blink necessarily means the viewer never consciously perceived T2.
claims.limitation: Accuracy reporting cannot uniquely establish conscious contents.

claims.claim: FV published Puységur archive contains critical evidence-trail discussion of somnambulism.
claims.limitation: Does not corroborate a magnetic healing mechanism.

claims.claim: FV has a published investigation of Franklin's 1784 mesmerism commission.
claims.limitation: Historical comparison only.

claims.claim: Existing free 52-page Focus Fieldbook remains one approved subscriber path.
claims.limitation: Do not add or modify Jetpack form.

claims.claim: Inspire3 lists Zen12, Hypnosis Live and Brainwave Shots.
claims.limitation: No implied independently evaluated efficacy.

claims.claim: Zen12 markets approximately twelve-minute sessions.
claims.limitation: Session duration not a clinical outcome.

claims.claim: Full Zen12 offer page lists twelve levels and 48 MP3 files.
claims.limitation: Package may differ by referral campaign.

claims.claim: Zen12 says twelve minutes is equivalent to an hour of meditation.
claims.limitation: No independent direct trial in reviewed record.

claims.claim: Zen12 audio is proven to improve focus, anxiety, health or money outcomes.
claims.limitation: Related science does not transfer to commercial SKU.

claims.claim: Hypnosis Live Total Focus is seller-listed as 33 min and 47 MB.
claims.limitation: No study proving focus gains.

claims.claim: Brainwave Focus Shot includes 15- and 30-min versions.
claims.limitation: Do not imply same offering as Zen12.

claims.claim: Brainwave Focus Shot creates hours of focused concentration.
claims.limitation: Vendor claim lacks product-specific adequate substantiation.

claims.claim: All Inspire3 affiliate publishers are automatically approved.
claims.limitation: Portal existence is not account acceptance.

claims.claim: Final Vestige has approved unique Zen12 affiliate URL and SKU rights.
claims.limitation: No authorization in verified Gmail results or issue.

claims.claim: Current checkout price/returns for Final Vestige referrals are established.

claims.claim: FV owned Mind paid product is live, rights-cleared, payable and fulfillable.

claims.claim: Affiliate material relationships need clear proximate disclosure.
